blocks.help: Adds a value to a collection: at the end of a list or deque, into a set, or into a queue, stack or priority queue.
Removes every item of a collection.
True when a list, deque or set holds the value, or a map has the key.

Runs blocks once for each item of a list, deque, set or text, in order. Read-only items can't be changed; a copy can, without changing the collection; an editable item changes the item in the collection.
Runs blocks once for each key of a map, smallest key first, with the key and its value. Neither can be changed.
True when a collection has no items.
The item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0), or the value for a key of a map. A position or key the collection does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
How many items a collection has.
A list, deque or set with these items. It takes its type from where it is plugged in, such as the value of a 'create' block whose type is chosen.
The item a queue, stack or priority queue gives next: the oldest of a queue, the newest of a stack, the largest of a priority queue. An empty one stops the program (debug builds report it).
Removes the item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0); the items after it move up. A position the list does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
Removes the item a queue, stack or priority queue gives next. An empty one stops the program (debug builds report it).
Removes a value from a set, or a key and its value from a map. Nothing happens when it is not there.

Changes the item at a position of a list or deque (the first is at 0), or sets the value for a key of a map, adding the key when the map does not have it yet. A position the list does not have stops the program with an out-of-range error.
Puts the items of a list or deque in order, smallest or largest first. The items must be comparable.
Leaves the innermost loop.
Skips the rest of this round of the innermost loop.
Counts from one number to another, running blocks for each value.
Repeats blocks forever (use stop or break to leave).
Runs blocks only when a condition is true. Add else if and else parts with ⊕, and remove them with ⊖.
Repeats blocks a number of times.
Repeats blocks while a condition is true; choose until in the menu to repeat until it becomes true.
Calls a function and uses its result.
Calls a function.
Defines a function: a named group of blocks you can use again.
Leaves the function, giving back a value if the function returns one.
Asks the user to type something and stores it in a variable.
Shows values in the console.
True or false.
True when the condition is false.
True when all (and) or any (or) of the conditions are true.
One of two values, depending on a condition.
Adds, subtracts, multiplies or divides two numbers, or gives the remainder.
Compares two values.
Converts a number to another number type, e.g. a decimal to a whole number.
A number, such as 42 or 3.14.
A random whole number between the two values, including both.
Ends the program. Exit code 0 means success.
The program starts here. A project has exactly one of these blocks.
A single character, such as 'a'.
Joins text and numbers into one piece of text.
A piece of text.
Adds to a variable (+=); choose down by (-=), times (*=), divided by (/=) or mod (%=) in the menu to subtract, multiply, divide or keep the remainder instead.
Creates a variable. It can be used by the blocks after it in the same place.
The value of a variable.
Gives a variable a new value.
